library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

Choi et al. (2024) built a translational, synapse-driven PK/PD model for
CD123-NKCE, a trifunctional natural killer cell engager that binds NKp46 and
CD16a on NK cells and CD123 on acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cells. The
translation runs in three steps, and each is a separate model here:

1. `Choi_2024_cd123nkce_invitro`: MOLM-13 cytotoxicity in vitro, which
   estimates the synapse parameters `kmax`, `EC50` and `gamma`.
2. `Choi_2024_cd123nkce_nhp`: PK, CD123+ cells and NKp46+ NK cells in healthy
   monkeys, with the synapse parameters carried over from step 1.
3. `Choi_2024_cd123nkce_human`: the projection to patients with AML that was
   used to select the first-in-human starting regimen.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Choi_2024_cd123nkce_human"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.13689> (open access; the model
  equations and the Monolix script for the AML model are in Appendix S1)

All three models share one structure. CD123-NKCE binds NKp46 on NK cells
(`drug_nkp46_central`) and CD123 on CD123+ cells (`drug_cd123_central`); either
binary complex then binds the other receptor to form the NKp46-drug-CD123
synapse (`trimer`). The synapse kills CD123+ cells at the Hill rate
`kmax * TBE^gamma / (EC50^gamma + TBE^gamma)`. Binding to CD16a is ignored
because its affinity is about 150-fold weaker than for NKp46. The in vivo
models add two-compartment PK, internalisation of drug-CD123 complexes, an
extra turned-over CD123 pool outside the blood (`target` / `complex`, the
main target-mediated drug sink), and synapse-driven redistribution of NK cells
out of the blood.

# Population

* **In vitro**: resting NK cells from two donors against 51Cr-labelled
  MOLM-13 cells at effector-to-target (E:T) ratios of 10:1, 5:1, 1:1 and 1:5
  (20 MOLM-13 cells/uL), eight drug concentrations from 1.5e-3 to 1.5e4 ng/mL,
  and incubations of 1, 4 and 20 h.
* **Monkeys**: 53 healthy animals in five studies (Table S1): IV 1-h infusions
  of 0.5-3000 ug/kg (single dose, weekly or twice weekly) and SC doses of
  3.6-3000 ug/kg. Twenty-three animals contributed PK and PD to the fit; the
  30 animals dosed twice weekly contributed PK only, and their PD data served
  as external validation.
* **AML patients**: a projection with no clinical data. Baseline NKp46+ NK
  cells were 54 cells/uL and CD123+ cells 1668 cells/uL (Table 1).

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Choi_2024_cd123nkce_nhp")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment that points to its source. The
table below collects them. "Table 1" is the main-text parameter table;
"Eq" numbers refer to Appendix S1, and "Table S2" is the Monolix script of the
AML model.

| Parameter (model name) | In vitro | Monkey | AML | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kmax` (1/h) | 0.332 (est.) | 0.332 (fixed) | 0.332 (fixed) | Table 1 |
| `EC50` (nM) | 1.46e-9 (est., IIV SD 0.998) | 1.46e-9 | 1.46e-9 | Table 1 |
| `gamma` (`hill`) | 1.04 (est.) | 1.04 | 1.04 | Table 1 |
| `kg` (1/h) | 0.0139 | 0.31 (IIV SD 0.83) | 0.0288 | Table 1 |
| `kout` NK (1/h) | -- | 0.2 | 0.002 | Table 1 |
| `KD1` NKp46 (nM) | 16.6 | 29 | 16.6 | Table 1 |
| `KD2` CD123 (nM) | 0.404 | 1.23 | 0.404 | Table 1 |
| `koff1`, `koff2` (1/s) | 0.001 | 0.001 | 0.001 | Table 1 |
| `RTdE` (`nkp46_receptors`) | 4600 | 4600 | 4600 | Table 1 |
| `RTdT` (`cd123_receptors`) | 4360 | 25,000 | 7000 | Table 1 |
| `EF0` (`rbase_nk`, cells/uL) | 4-200 (per well) | median 247 | 54 | Table 1 |
| `TC0` (`rbase_cd123`, cells/uL) | 20 | median 28 | 1668 | Table 1 |
| `CL` (mL/h/kg) | -- | 0.32 (IIV SD 0.20) | 0.18 | Table 1 |
| `Q` (mL/h/kg) | -- | 1.35 | 0.37 | Table 1 |
| `V1` (L/kg) | -- | 0.040 (IIV SD 0.130) | 0.042 | Table 1 |
| `V2` (L/kg) | -- | 0.020 (IIV SD 0.26) | 0.031 | Table 1 |
| `ka` (1/h) | -- | 0.04 | -- | Table 1 |
| `F` | -- | 74.0% (logit IIV SD 0.28) | -- | Table 1 |
| `kint` (1/h) | -- | 0.15 | 0.15 | Table 1 |
| `kinTP` (`ksyn`, nM/h) | -- | 0.21 (IIV SD 0.57) | 0.21 | Table 1 |
| `alpha` (`target_scale`, nM) | -- | 19.44 (IIV SD 0.61) | 19.44 | Table 1 |
| `beta` (`target_exp`) | -- | 0.21 | 0.21 | Table 1 |
| `SlpNK` (`slope_nk`) | -- | 5.72 | 5.72 | Table 1 |
| `TADA` (h) | -- | 333 (IIV SD 0.20) | -- | Table 1 |
| `KADA` (1/h) | -- | 1.94 (IIV SD 4.21) | -- | Table 1 |
| `ktol` (1/h) | -- | 0.0032 (IIV SD 1.63) | -- | Table 1 |
| `delta` (`delta_tol`) | -- | 0.18 (IIV SD 0.53) | -- | Table 1 |
| `TCmax` (cells/uL) | -- | -- | 3252 | Table 1 |
| Molecular weight (g/mol) | -- | 149,000 | 149,000 | Table S2 |
| Avogadro's number | 6.022e14 /nmol | same | same | Table S2 |
| Binding ODEs | Eqs 1-4 | Eqs 2, 4, 14-17 | Table S2 | Appendix S1 |
| Killing rate | Eq 8 | Eq 8 | Table S2 `kel` | Appendix S1 |
| Free receptors `E`, `T` | Eqs 9-10 | Table S2 | Table S2 | Appendix S1 |
| Non-blood CD123 baseline `TP0` | -- | Eq 18 | Table S2 | Appendix S1 |
| NK redistribution | -- | Eq 19 | Table S2 `ddt_EF` | Appendix S1 |
| CD123+ growth | Eqs 6-7 | Eqs 20-21 (tolerance) | Table S2 `ddt_TA` (logistic) | Appendix S1 |
| ADA switch | -- | Eq 14 | -- | Appendix S1 |

The IIV column of Table 1 reports the standard deviation of each random
effect, so the `ini()` variances are its squares. All random effects are
log-normal except `F`, which is logit-normal (Table 1 footnote p).

# In vitro cytotoxicity (Figure 3)

The in vitro model is deterministic apart from the inter-experiment variability
on `EC50`, which is zeroed here to reproduce the typical curves of Figure 3.
The drug concentration enters as an `amt` in nM at time 0. Figure 3 plots the
concentration in ng/mL, and Table 1 gives the same range as 1.02e-5 to
102 nM, so ng/mL is converted with that ratio (102 / 1.5e4, i.e. a molecular
weight of about 147 kDa).

```{r invitro-sim}
mod_iv <- readModelDb("Choi_2024_cd123nkce_invitro") |> rxode2::zeroRe()

conc_ngml <- 1.5 * 10^(-3:4)
et_design <- tibble::tibble(
  et_label = factor(c("10:1", "5:1", "1:1", "1:5"), levels = c("10:1", "5:1", "1:1", "1:5")),
  rbase_nk = c(200, 100, 20, 4)
)
wells <- tidyr::expand_grid(et_design, conc_ngml = conc_ngml) |>
  mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())

iv_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  wells |> mutate(time = 0, amt = conc_ngml * 102 / 1.5e4, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(wells, time = c(1, 4, 20)) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim_iv <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_iv,
  events = iv_events,
  keep = c("et_label", "conc_ngml"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 6}
sim_iv |>
  ggplot(aes(conc_ngml, cytotox, colour = et_label)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  facet_grid(et_label ~ paste(time, "h")) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "CD123-NKCE (ng/mL)", y = "Cytotoxicity (%)", colour = "E:T",
    caption = "Replicates the typical model curves of Figure 3 of Choi 2024."
  )
```

The curves reproduce Figure 3: killing rises with E:T ratio and incubation
time, and every panel is bell-shaped, because at the highest concentrations
both receptors are saturated by binary complexes and fewer synapses form.

## The free-CD123 term

Appendix S1 Eq 10 writes the total CD123 pool from the *baseline* target-cell
count `TC0`, and the text says that "the number of cells remains constant in
vitro". The Monolix script of the AML model (Table S2) instead uses the
current target-cell count (`TC = TA * RTdT`). The packaged model uses the
current, surviving-cell count. The comparison below shows why: with the
published estimates, only that form reproduces the typical curves of Figure 3.
The reference values were read by the maintainers from Figure 3 and are
accurate to a few percentage points.

```{r invitro-eq10}
fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~et_label, ~time, ~conc_ngml, ~fig3,
  "10:1", 1, 150, 22,
  "10:1", 4, 150, 62,
  "10:1", 20, 15000, 85,
  "5:1", 20, 150, 95,
  "5:1", 20, 15000, 78,
  "1:1", 4, 150, 33,
  "1:1", 20, 150, 77,
  "1:1", 20, 15000, 45,
  "1:5", 20, 150, 43,
  "1:5", 20, 15000, 15
)

# The printed Eq 10: total CD123 fixed at the baseline cell count.
mod_iv_eq10 <- readModelDb("Choi_2024_cd123nkce_invitro") |>
  rxode2::model(
    tfree <- rbase_cd123 * cd123_receptors * 1e6 / navo - drug_cd123_central - trimer
  ) |>
  rxode2::zeroRe()
sim_iv_eq10 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_iv_eq10,
  events = iv_events,
  keep = c("et_label", "conc_ngml"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)

lookup <- function(sim, et, tm, cc) {
  v <- sim$cytotox[as.character(sim$et_label) == et & sim$time == tm & abs(sim$conc_ngml - cc) < 1e-6 * cc]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique row for ", et, " / ", tm, " h / ", cc, " ng/mL")
  v
}
fig3_check <- fig3 |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    packaged = lookup(sim_iv, et_label, time, conc_ngml),
    printed_eq10 = lookup(sim_iv_eq10, et_label, time, conc_ngml)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

fig3_check |>
  mutate(across(c(packaged, printed_eq10), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "E:T" = et_label, "Time (h)" = time, "Concentration (ng/mL)" = conc_ngml,
    "Figure 3 (%)" = fig3, "Packaged model (%)" = packaged,
    "Printed Eq 10 (%)" = printed_eq10
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  nrow(fig3_check) == 10L,
  # The packaged form sits within the reading accuracy of the figure.
  max(abs(fig3_check$packaged - fig3_check$fig3)) < 6,
  # The printed Eq 10 misses the 20-h panels by more than 10 points.
  max(abs(fig3_check$printed_eq10 - fig3_check$fig3)) > 10
)
```

# Monkey PK/PD (Figure 4)

## Deterministic checks

The paper states that, at the median baseline of 28 CD123+ cells/uL, the
blood CD123 pool is 0.0011 nM and the non-blood pool is 4.70 nM
(Discussion). Both follow from Eq 18 and the Table 1 values, and the typical
model reproduces them as the steady state before dosing.

```{r nhp-tp0}
mod_nhp <- readModelDb("Choi_2024_cd123nkce_nhp")
mod_nhp_typ <- mod_nhp |> rxode2::zeroRe()

sim_pre <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_nhp_typ,
  events = rxode2::et(c(0, 24, 168)),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
blood_cd123_0 <- 28 * 25000 * 1e6 / 6.022e14
c(blood_nM = blood_cd123_0, nonblood_nM = sim_pre$target[1])
stopifnot(
  abs(blood_cd123_0 / 0.0011 - 1) < 0.06,
  abs(sim_pre$target[1] / 4.70 - 1) < 0.01,
  # No dose: the non-blood pool and the cell counts stay at baseline.
  max(abs(sim_pre$target / sim_pre$target[1] - 1)) < 1e-4,
  max(abs(sim_pre$cd123cell_central / 28 - 1)) < 1e-4
)
```

A 3000 ug/kg IV dose is 20.1 nmol/kg, which in the 0.040 L/kg central volume
is 503 nM before any binding or elimination. The simulated end-of-infusion
concentration sits just below that, as in Figure 4a (about 500 nM).

```{r nhp-cmax}
ev_3000 <- rxode2::et(amt = 3000, time = 0, cmt = "central", dur = 1) |>
  rxode2::et(c(0.5, 1, 2, 24))
sim_3000 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_nhp_typ, events = ev_3000, returnType = "data.frame")
c0 <- 3000 * 1e3 / 149000 / 0.040
cmax_typ <- sim_3000$Cc[sim_3000$time == 1]
c(closed_form_nM = c0, simulated_eoi_nM = cmax_typ)
stopifnot(cmax_typ < c0, cmax_typ / c0 > 0.9)
```

## Visual predictive check

```{r nhp-cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240103)
n_per_arm <- 50L

h <- function(days) days * 24
nhp_arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                ~route,    ~dose,  ~dose_days,
  "IV 3000 SD",        "IV",      3000,   list(0),
  "IV 100 QW",         "IV",      100,    list(c(0, 7, 14, 21)),
  "IV 3000 QW",        "IV",      3000,   list(c(0, 7, 14, 21)),
  "SC 3.6 SD",         "SC",      3.6,    list(0),
  "IV 100 b.i.w.",     "IV",      100,    list(c(0, 3, 7, 10, 14, 17, 21, 24, 28)),
  "IV 3000 b.i.w.",    "IV",      3000,   list(c(0, 3, 7, 10, 14, 17, 21, 24, 28)),
  "SC 3000 b.i.w.",    "SC",      3000,   list(c(0, 3, 7, 10, 14, 17, 21, 24, 28))
) |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arm), arm_index = dplyr::row_number())

obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.25), seq(3, 48, by = 3), seq(48, h(49), by = 12))))

make_arm <- function(arm_row) {
  ids <- (arm_row$arm_index - 1L) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = h(unlist(arm_row$dose_days))) |>
    mutate(
      evid = 1L, amt = arm_row$dose,
      cmt = if (arm_row$route == "IV") "central" else "depot",
      dur = if (arm_row$route == "IV") 1 else 0
    )
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dur = 0)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(arm = arm_row$arm)
}
nhp_events <- lapply(split(nhp_arms, nhp_arms$arm), make_arm) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(nhp_events[nhp_events$evid == 1L, c("id", "time")]))

sim_nhp <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_nhp,
  events = nhp_events,
  keep = c("arm"),
  returnType = "data.frame",
  cores = 1L
)
```

```{r figure-4a, fig.height = 6}
vpc <- function(sim, var) {
  sim |>
    group_by(arm, time) |>
    summarise(
      Q05 = quantile(.data[[var]], 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
      Q50 = quantile(.data[[var]], 0.50, na.rm = TRUE),
      Q95 = quantile(.data[[var]], 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
vpc(sim_nhp, "Cc") |>
  mutate(across(c(Q05, Q50, Q95), \(x) pmax(x, 1e-3))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "pink", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~arm, ncol = 4) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Free CD123-NKCE (nM)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4a of Choi 2024: median and 90% prediction interval; floored at 1e-3 nM."
  )
```

```{r figure-4bc, fig.height = 6}
sd_qw_arms <- c("IV 3000 SD", "IV 100 QW", "IV 3000 QW", "SC 3.6 SD")
dplyr::bind_rows(
  vpc(sim_nhp, "cd123cell_central") |> mutate(panel = "CD123+ cells (cells/uL)"),
  vpc(sim_nhp, "nkcell_central") |> mutate(panel = "NKp46+ NK cells (cells/uL)")
) |>
  filter(arm %in% sd_qw_arms) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "pink", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  facet_grid(panel ~ arm, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figures 4b and 4c of Choi 2024: median and 90% prediction interval."
  )
```

The simulations reproduce the main features of Figure 4. After 3000 ug/kg IV
the concentration starts near 500 nM. It collapses around day 14, when
anti-drug antibodies emerge (`TADA` = 333 h). From then on the model adds the
`KADA` elimination and stops delivering further doses. That is why the third
and fourth weekly doses barely register in the median. CD123+ cells are
depleted within a day and recover once the drug is gone. NK cells fall during
synapse formation and return to baseline.

The CD123+ rebound in this model overshoots baseline and then oscillates. That
comes from the moderator-mediated tolerance term: growth is driven by
`kg * (1 - (M/TC0)^delta)`, and the moderator `M` lags the cell count with a
9-day half-life, so the cells overshoot before `M` catches up. Individual fits
in Figure S1 show the same overshoot-and-return pattern. With the large IIV on
`kg` and `ktol`, the population median smooths the oscillation.

The NK-cell prediction interval is narrower than in Figure 4c. The paper used
each animal's own baseline (144-1110 cells/uL) as a regressor, whereas these
simulations hold every animal at the median baseline of 247 cells/uL.

```{r nhp-assert}
med_at <- function(var, arm_name, t_h) {
  v <- sim_nhp[[var]][sim_nhp$arm == arm_name & sim_nhp$time == t_h]
  if (length(v) != n_per_arm) stop("expected ", n_per_arm, " rows for ", arm_name, " at ", t_h, " h")
  median(v)
}
stopifnot(
  # IV 3000 SD: median end-of-infusion concentration within 15% of 500 nM
  abs(med_at("Cc", "IV 3000 SD", 1) / 500 - 1) < 0.15,
  # CD123+ cells are depleted by more than 80% at 24 h in the median
  med_at("cd123cell_central", "IV 3000 SD", 24) < 0.2 * 28,
  # NK cells are back to within 10% of baseline 7 weeks after a single dose
  abs(med_at("nkcell_central", "IV 3000 SD", h(48)) / 247 - 1) < 0.1
)
```

# Projection to patients with AML (Figure 5)

The paper looked for a starting regimen that met two criteria. First, the
concentration at the end of the first infusion should stay below 1.7 nM, the
lowest concentration that caused mild cytokine release in a whole-blood assay.
Second, CD123+ cells should fall by more than 95% within the first 28-day
cycle. Figure 5 compares a flat 100 ug/kg twice-weekly regimen with an
intrapatient escalation of 10 and 30 ug/kg in week 1 followed by 100 ug/kg.
Figure 5 draws doses on days 0, 3, 7, 10, 14 and 21, and that schedule is used
here. The model has no variability, so these are typical-value solves. The
Monolix script delivers each dose as a 0.0001-h input, which is equivalent to
an IV bolus.

```{r aml-sim}
mod_aml <- readModelDb("Choi_2024_cd123nkce_human")
dose_days <- c(0, 3, 7, 10, 14, 21)
aml_regimens <- list(
  "Flat 100" = rep(100, 6),
  "10/30/100" = c(10, 30, 100, 100, 100, 100)
)
aml_obs <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(0, h(28), by = 0.5))))
aml_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(aml_regimens), function(i) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(id = i, time = h(dose_days), amt = aml_regimens[[i]], evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
    tibble::tibble(id = i, time = aml_obs, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    mutate(regimen = names(aml_regimens)[i])
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim_aml <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_aml, events = aml_events, keep = c("regimen"), returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r figure-5a}
sim_aml |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Cc, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1.7, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Free CD123-NKCE (nM)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5a of Choi 2024; dashed line: 1.7 nM cytokine-release threshold."
  )
```

```{r figure-5b}
sim_aml |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, cd123_pctcfb, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0, -95), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Change from baseline in CD123+ cells (%)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5b of Choi 2024."
  )
```

The values below are compared with readings the maintainers took from
Figure 5. They are accurate to roughly a factor of 1.5 on the logarithmic PK
axis and to a few percentage points on the linear change-from-baseline axis.

```{r aml-check}
aml_at <- function(reg, t_h, var) {
  v <- sim_aml[[var]][sim_aml$regimen == reg & abs(sim_aml$time - t_h) < 1e-9]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique row for ", reg, " at ", t_h, " h")
  v
}
first_peak <- function(reg) max(sim_aml$Cc[sim_aml$regimen == reg & sim_aml$time > 0 & sim_aml$time <= 2])

fig5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~regimen, ~figure5, ~simulated,
  "Peak after first dose (nM)", "Flat 100", 8, first_peak("Flat 100"),
  "Peak after first dose (nM)", "10/30/100", 0.07, first_peak("10/30/100"),
  "Trough before day-3 dose (nM)", "Flat 100", 6e-3, aml_at("Flat 100", h(3) - 0.5, "Cc"),
  "Trough before day-3 dose (nM)", "10/30/100", 2e-5, aml_at("10/30/100", h(3) - 0.5, "Cc"),
  "Concentration on day 28 (nM)", "Flat 100", 1.5e-3, aml_at("Flat 100", h(28), "Cc"),
  "CD123+ change at day 1 (%)", "10/30/100", -92, aml_at("10/30/100", h(1), "cd123_pctcfb"),
  "CD123+ change before day-3 dose (%)", "10/30/100", -75, aml_at("10/30/100", h(3) - 0.5, "cd123_pctcfb"),
  "CD123+ change on day 28 (%)", "Flat 100", -96.5, aml_at("Flat 100", h(28), "cd123_pctcfb")
)
fig5 |>
  mutate(
    figure5 = vapply(figure5, \(x) format(x, trim = TRUE), character(1)),
    simulated = vapply(simulated, \(x) format(signif(x, 3), trim = TRUE), character(1))
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("Quantity" = quantity, "Regimen" = regimen, "Figure 5" = figure5, "Simulated" = simulated) |>
  knitr::kable()

pk_rows <- grepl("nM", fig5$quantity)
stopifnot(
  # PK readings within a factor of 2 on the log axis
  all(abs(log(fig5$simulated[pk_rows] / fig5$figure5[pk_rows])) < log(2)),
  # Change-from-baseline readings within 5 percentage points
  all(abs(fig5$simulated[!pk_rows] - fig5$figure5[!pk_rows]) < 5)
)
```

The two dose-selection criteria hold as the paper reports. The flat 100 ug/kg
regimen exceeds 1.7 nM at the first dose. The 10 ug/kg first dose peaks about
one log unit below the threshold. Both regimens reduce CD123+ cells by more
than 95% during the first cycle. "Peak" here is the highest free
concentration after the first few minutes, which is what Figure 5 plots.
Immediately after the bolus, before any binding, the concentration is simply
dose / V1: 16 nM for 100 ug/kg and 1.6 nM for 10 ug/kg (see the NCA below).
Binding to the 8.5 nM non-blood CD123 pool removes most of a 10 ug/kg dose
within minutes.

```{r aml-criteria}
cfb_min <- sim_aml |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(nadir = min(cd123_pctcfb), day28 = cd123_pctcfb[time == h(28)], .groups = "drop")
cfb_min
stopifnot(
  first_peak("Flat 100") > 1.7,
  first_peak("10/30/100") < 1.7 / 10,
  all(cfb_min$nadir < -95),
  all(cfb_min$day28 < -95)
)
```

# PKNCA

The paper reports no NCA parameters, so there is no published table to
compare against. The NCA below summarises the simulated exposure, grouped by
arm, over the first dosing interval of each scenario. For the monkeys, that
covers the single-dose arms (0-168 h, before anti-drug antibodies emerge). For
the patients with AML, it is the first 72 h of each regimen, up to but not
including the second dose.

```{r pknca-nhp}
nca_nhp_conc <- sim_nhp |>
  filter(arm %in% c("IV 3000 SD", "SC 3.6 SD"), time <= 168, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, arm)
nca_nhp_conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nca_nhp_conc,
  nca_nhp_conc |> dplyr::distinct(id, arm) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, arm, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, arm, time)
# Concentrations may undershoot zero by integrator noise in the far tail.
stopifnot(all(nca_nhp_conc$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(nca_nhp_conc$Cc)))
nca_nhp_conc$Cc <- pmax(nca_nhp_conc$Cc, 0)

nca_nhp_dose <- nhp_events |>
  filter(evid == 1L, arm %in% c("IV 3000 SD", "SC 3.6 SD")) |>
  select(id, time, amt, arm) |>
  mutate(arm = as.character(arm))
nca_nhp_conc$arm <- as.character(nca_nhp_conc$arm)

nca_nhp <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_nhp_conc, Cc ~ time | arm + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_nhp_dose, amt ~ time | arm + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 168, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))
nca_nhp_summary <- summary(nca_nhp)
knitr::kable(nca_nhp_summary, caption = "Simulated monkey NCA, 0-168 h (geometric mean and CV).")
```

```{r pknca-aml}
nca_aml_conc <- sim_aml |>
  filter(time < 72, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, regimen)
nca_aml_dose <- aml_events |>
  filter(evid == 1L, time == 0) |>
  select(id, time, amt, regimen)
nca_aml <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_aml_conc, Cc ~ time | regimen + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_aml_dose, amt ~ time | regimen + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 72, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))
nca_aml_res <- as.data.frame(nca_aml$result)
nca_aml_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast")) |>
  select(regimen, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "Cmax (nM)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-72 (nM*h)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

nca_val <- function(reg, param) {
  v <- nca_aml_res$PPORRES[nca_aml_res$regimen == reg & nca_aml_res$PPTESTCD == param]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique ", param, " for ", reg)
  v
}
# Cmax is the post-bolus concentration dose * 1e3 / MW / V1.
cmax_closed <- c("Flat 100" = 100, "10/30/100" = 10) * 1e3 / 149000 / 0.042
auc_ratio <- nca_val("Flat 100", "auclast") / nca_val("10/30/100", "auclast")
auc_ratio
stopifnot(
  abs(nca_val("Flat 100", "cmax") / cmax_closed[["Flat 100"]] - 1) < 1e-3,
  abs(nca_val("10/30/100", "cmax") / cmax_closed[["10/30/100"]] - 1) < 1e-3,
  # Target-mediated disposition: a 10-fold dose ratio gives a much larger
  # exposure ratio.
  auc_ratio > 20
)
```

Cmax equals dose / V1 for both regimens, because the doses are boluses. The
target-mediated sink shows in the exposure instead: a 10-fold lower first
dose gives a far more than 10-fold lower AUC over the first 72 h, because the
non-blood CD123 pool binds most of a small dose.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Free-CD123 term in the in vitro model.** Appendix S1 Eq 10 computes total
  CD123 from the baseline cell count `TC0`. The packaged model uses the
  surviving treated-cell count, as the Monolix script of the AML model does,
  because only that form reproduces the typical curves of Figure 3 with the
  published estimates (see the comparison table above).
* **Printed typos corrected.** In Appendix S1, Eq 3 (in vitro `dTB/dt`) has
  `kon2*T*E` as its first term, and Eq 4 has `+koff1*TBE`. Both were taken in
  the mass-balanced forms of Table S2 (`kon2*T*B` and `-koff1*TBE`). The
  undefined `kinttb` in the Table S2 `ddt_TAP` line was taken as `kint`, per
  Eq 17. Eq 21's initial condition is printed as `TC(0) = TC0`; it is taken as
  `M(0) = TC0`, as in Table S2 (`M_0 = TA0`). The Results text gives a
  "14-h" NK half-life, but Table 1 (`kout` = 0.002 1/h) and the Discussion
  both correspond to 14 days; the Table 1 value is used.
* **NK-redistribution exponent.** Table S2 raises the synapse to an exponent
  `nNK` that Table 1 does not list. Appendix S1 Eq 19 has no exponent, so
  `nNK` = 1.
* **Monkey baselines.** The paper used each animal's observed NK and CD123+
  baseline as a regressor. The model carries the cohort medians (247 and 28
  cells/uL) as fixed parameters; set `rbase_nk` and `rbase_cd123` per subject
  through `rxSolve(params = )` to reproduce the individual-baseline form.
  Likewise, the in vitro NK concentration `rbase_nk` defaults to the 10:1 E:T
  arm and is set per well.
* **Anti-drug antibody switch.** Appendix S1 Eq 14 replaces the IV and SC
  inputs with 1e-9 after `TADA`. The packaged model sets them to zero:
  doses given after `TADA` deliver nothing, and the SC depot stops feeding
  the central compartment.
* **Monkey IV infusion and molecular weight.** All monkey IV doses were 1-h
  infusions (Table S1), and the simulations above use `dur = 1`. The monkey
  PK uses the 149 kDa molecular weight of the AML script, which the paper
  does not restate for the monkey model. It reproduces the about 500 nM
  end-of-infusion concentration of Figure 4a.
* **Residual error.** The paper does not report residual-error estimates for
  any of the three models, so none is included. The models simulate typical
  or individual predictions only. Monkey PK and CD123+ data below the limit of
  quantification were handled with the M3 method in the original fit.
* **AML regimen schedule.** Figure 5 is labelled twice weekly but draws doses
  on days 0, 3, 7, 10, 14 and 21; that schedule is used.
* **Species label.** The paper refers to the animals only as monkeys /
  nonhuman primates and does not name the species.
